audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart said 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet chart both read Sylas/Sylas/Sylas/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Sylas — the page rendered two different answers per row.
audit.why: Sylas wins 1-3 on Chain Lash (Q) range 775 plus the Kingslayer (W) heal; Fizz takes 6 and first item because Chum the Waters grounds both his dashes; Sylas retakes late as Hijack falls to 30s.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side -> Sylas, phases[4..5].side -> Fizz, phases[6].side -> Sylas, whys rewritten to match; content win[] already correct so no win[N] edit is needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] and late credited Sylas's self-heal to Petricite Burst (W); spikes[1] said Hijack steals 'whichever ult he's hit most recently' and could take your Playful/Trickster.
audit.why: Petricite Burst is the passive (attack-speed + chain damage). The heal is Kingslayer (W), 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s. Hijack (80/55/30s) steals the ultimate of the champion it is cast on — never a basic ability.
audit.corrected: Heal attributed to Kingslayer (W); Hijack described as targeting a champion's ultimate on an 80s rank-1 cooldown, dropping to 30s at rank 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Fizz's Playful/Trickster (E) and Chum the Waters (R) both ground, and Sylas's only mobility is two dashes.
audit.why: Kingslayer (W) and Abscond/Abduct (E) are both flagged dash; grounding denies them. Abscond is 13s at rank 1 and is his only escape. Kingslayer heals, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, dos, donts, ahead, feeding and carry now say: ground the dash, anti-heal the W, step up on a spent Abscond.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Body did not match the title.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles using the grounding and E-cooldown facts.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Sylas

edits.before: W-empowered last hits and short Q trades — your passive ignores minion block, so fish through the wave freely.
edits.after: Chain Lash (Q) outranges you at 775 and his passive chip beats your W bleed — last-hit, take no extended trade.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Sylas

edits.before: Q-W trade pattern live: dash through, bleed, walk out through the wave nobody else can walk through.
edits.after: Kingslayer (W) heals off you every 12s at rank 1, so he wins the level 2 all-in — trade only on a whiffed Q.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Sylas

edits.before: E online — the troll pole changes everything: you now dodge one full rotation per fight and they know it.
edits.after: Playful/Trickster is up, but his Q-E-W burst plus heal still wins a straight level 3 fight — pole it, don't trade.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Fizz

edits.before: Chum the Waters online — the shark plus full string deletes most mids from 70%. The lane is now a horror film.
edits.after: Chum the Waters grounds and knocks up — he cannot Abscond out of it, and Hijack is only up every 80s at rank 1.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Fizz

edits.before: First item spike: the string one-shots squishies who eat the shark. Fish aggressively.
edits.after: First item: R-Q-W-E kills him through Kingslayer if your anti-heal is up. Fish aggressively.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Sylas

edits.before: Late Fizz erases one carry per fight: shark the entry, string the target, pole the response, swim away.
edits.after: Late Hijack is up every 30s — he steals a fight-winning ult and heals through your burst, so pick, don't duel.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Playful / Trickster has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Abscond/Abduct (E): 13s at rank 1 and his only escape — step up the second it is spent. - Kingslayer (W): a 12s heal-dash that Grievous Wounds blanks. - Your Playful/Trickster is 16s at rank 1: hold it to ground his Abduct, never to open.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Abduct is his engage and his exit; once it is used he has 13s with no escape — that is your window.

edits.before: Q through him, W bleed, walk out through the wave — the fish phases in and out before his answer finds a target.
edits.after: Playful/Trickster grounds Abscond and Kingslayer — hop as he commits and he is stranded with a 13s escape down.

edits.before: Sylas whiffs Abscond / Abduct and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Throw the shark as he dashes in — grounding denies the Abduct exit.

edits.before: Hopping in first against a held CC — the pole spent as an entrance is the whole kit spent as a coin flip.
edits.after: Spending E as an entrance leaves you inside Chain Lash with 16s before the untargetable window returns.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Sylas wins by Abducting you onto his Chain Lash, refunding the trade with Kingslayer, and stealing Chum the Waters at 6.

edits.before: Ahead, fish openly: zone Sylas with string threat, shark every river, and pole the counterplay — fed Fizz makes the map an aquarium.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: anti-heal blunts Kingslayer, the shark grounds his Abduct, and a Sylas with no escape gives up plates and river.

edits.before: If Sylas opens the score, reset expectations and respect Abscond / Abduct doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W last-hits and stay relevant through pole plays.
edits.after: If Sylas opens the score, Kingslayer's heal scales with his lead and the lane sours fast — farm with W last-hits, buy Grievous Wounds early, and only step up once Abscond is spent.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — shark, string, pole, repeat; one carry per fight is the contract and the pole notarizes it.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before Kingslayer refunds it — anti-heal first, shark to ground the exit, then string him down.

edits.before: Sylas has full-combo burst plus a self-heal from Petricite Burst (W) built in from level 3, so he wins early skirmishes even when you land your own damage back on him.
edits.after: Sylas has full-combo burst plus the Kingslayer (W) heal from level 3, and that heal refunds more the lower his health, so he wins early skirmishes even when you damage him back.

edits.before: His ultimate steals whichever enemy ult he's hit most recently — if he's already stolen your Playful/Trickster or another team's engage, he can flip fights instantly, so this level is a coinflip depending on what he's picked up.
edits.after: Hijack steals the ultimate of whichever champion he casts it on — your Chum the Waters, or a stronger engage from elsewhere on your team — and at rank 1 it is only up every 80 seconds, so this level swings on what he took.

edits.before: Level 6 favors him since Hijack can steal a game-changing ultimate to flip fights
edits.after: Level 6 favors you — the shark grounds his dashes, so he cannot Abscond out of it

edits.before: Your first item spike (Riftmaker/Nashor's) actually closes the burst gap and lets Fizz's mobility dictate engages instead of just reacting to his, giving you the edge in that window. But by full build Sylas's Hijack pick potential and innate lifesteal-sustain from Petricite Burst catch back up, so the very late game swings back to being his to press if he's found a good ultimate to steal.
edits.after: Your first item spike (Riftmaker/Nashor's) actually closes the burst gap and lets Fizz's mobility dictate engages instead of just reacting to his, giving you the edge in that window. But by full build Hijack is up every 30 seconds and the Kingslayer heal scales with his AP, so the very late game swings back to being his to press if he's found a good ultimate to steal.

notes: Full-layer phases[N].side was 'Skill' on every row while content win[N] already matched the packet levelChart; I moved the full layer onto the content layer's verdicts, so no paired win[N] edit was required (win[] is already correct). content 'mid' still calls level 6 a coinflip and levels 4-5 'rough for you' while win[4]=Fizz and win[3]=Skill; I left it rather than force a same-length rewrite of a long paragraph — worth a second pass. Sylas is male, pronouns correct throughout. Confirmed from the kit: Abscond/Abduct 13/12/11/10/9s, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s (both dashes, so both deniable by Fizz's E and R grounding), Hijack 80/55/30s. Petricite Burst is the passive, not the heal — that error appeared twice in the content layer.
